def jitter_within_ten_percent(delay):
    """Return an integer jittered delay within +/-10% of the input delay.
    For delay <= 0, return 0. Uses integer arithmetic and rounds half down.
    Jitter = delay - delay//20 + (delay//10 - delay//20) to ensure symmetry.
    Example: jitter_within_ten_percent(100) -> 95."""
    if delay <= 0:
        return 0
    lower = delay - delay // 20
    upper = delay + delay // 10
    span = upper - lower
    offset = span // 2
    return lower + offset

print(jitter_within_ten_percent(2))

function.name: update_verification_session
function.description: Updates mutable fields of an existing verification session, such as the callback URL or verification type (if still pending). Cannot alter identity data or change status directly; side effect: triggers a re-evaluation of the session if type is changed.

verification_type.description: New verification level (only if session is pending).

function.name: list_verification_sessions
function.description: Returns a paginated list of verification sessions for a given user, filtered by optional status. Useful for audit or user history; read-only.

user_id.description: The user whose verification sessions to list.

function.name: fetch_identity_summary
function.description: Retrieves a verified user's identity profile summary (name, date of birth, address) after successful verification. Requires an approved session; returns consolidated data from the last successful verification, not just a session status.

user_id.description: The user to fetch identity summary for.

include_address.description: If true, includes the user's registered address in the response.

function.name: create_verification_session
function.description: Starts a new identity verification session for a user, generating a unique session ID and returning a verification URL for the user to complete KYC flow. This is a write operation and will store the session with a default 24-hour expiry; subsequent checks on this session will reflect its state.

user_id.description: The unique identifier of the user initiating the verification.

callback_url.description: URL to receive async notifications when the session status changes.

function.name: get_verification_status
function.description: Retrieves the current status and details of a specific verification session, including any rejection reasons or document flags. Read-only; does not modify the session.

session_id.description: The unique identifier of the verification session, as returned by create_verification_session.

include_documents.description: If true, includes uploaded document metadata in the response.

function.name: submit_verification_document
function.description: Uploads a document (e.g., passport, driver's license) to an existing verification session for identity proofing. This is a write operation; the document must be a valid image or PDF, and the session must be in 'pending' status.

session_id.description: The session to attach the document to.

document_type.description: The type of identity document being submitted.

document_data.description: Base64-encoded content of the document file.

expiry_date.description: Document expiry date in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).

function.name: delete_verification_session
function.description: Permanently deletes a verification session and all associated identity data from the system. This is irreversible; use only for cancelled or erroneous sessions. Side effect: any pending documents are purged.

reason.description: Optional reason for deletion, stored for audit logs.

STANDARD TRAVEL INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by VoyagerGuard Assurance


1. DEFINITIONS AND GENERAL TERMS
  1.1 If you are not satisfied with any decision or response from us, you may submit a formal complaint in writing to our complaints department. We will acknowledge your complaint within a reasonable time and investigate it thoroughly. If you remain unhappy, you may refer the matter to the relevant financial ombudsman service.
  1.2 We will use the personal information you provide solely to administer your policy and to process any requests you make. Your data will be stored securely and will not be shared with third parties except as required by law or with your explicit consent. You have the right to request a copy of the data we hold about you.
  1.3 To contact us, please use the telephone number and email address printed on your policy schedule. Our customer service team is available to answer questions during normal business hours in the country where your policy was issued. You may also write to our registered office address, which is listed on our website.

2. COVERAGE AND LIMITS
  2.1 The scheme covers the following categories:
  - Trip Cancellation: This covers non-refundable prepaid trip costs if you must cancel due to sudden illness, injury, or a family emergency before departure. Per-claim limit: €500.
  - Medical Expenses: This covers emergency medical treatment and hospital care abroad caused by an accident or sudden sickness during your trip. Per-claim limit: €250.
  - Baggage and Personal Effects: This covers loss, theft, or accidental damage to your luggage and personal belongings while traveling. Per-claim limit: €500.
  - Travel Delay: This covers reasonable additional accommodation and meal costs if your scheduled transport is delayed for a covered reason beyond your control. Per-claim limit: €5,000.
  2.2 The per-claim limit is applied to the loss first; the deductible of €500 is then subtracted from the capped amount.
  2.3 The policyholder bears 10% of the amount remaining after the deductible and limit; the provider pays the rest.
  2.4 Total payments in one policy year may not exceed €12,000; amounts already paid in the year reduce what remains.

3. EXCLUSIONS
  3.1 We will not cover any claim arising from a medical condition for which you received treatment or medication within the twelve months before your travel start date.
  3.2 We will not cover any loss or injury resulting from your participation in extreme sports or activities that are not listed as covered in the policy schedule.
  3.3 We will not cover any claim if you booked your trip after an official government travel warning for your destination was issued.
  3.4 We will not cover any claim that arises while you are engaged in any activity that is illegal under the laws of your destination or home country.

4. CONDITIONS
  4.1 Nothing is payable for a loss occurring fewer than 30 days after the inception date.
  4.2 A claim must be notified within 14 days after the loss date; later notification is not accepted.
  4.3 Every claim must be accompanied by the police report.

5. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURE
  Each claim is assessed in this order and the first applicable step decides it: (a) waiting period (4.1), (b) notification deadline (4.2), (c) exclusions (Section 3; the lowest-numbered applicable exclusion is named), (d) documentation (4.3: the claim is held, not denied), (e) amount (Section 2), (f) any amount above €2,000 requires senior-adjuster sign-off before payment.

6. PRECEDENCE
  If any other part of these terms conflicts with Section 3 or Section 5, Sections 3 and 5 prevail.
  Only the person named as the policyholder may submit a request under this scheme. If you are acting on behalf of the policyholder, you must provide written authorization from them. We may ask for proof of identity before processing any request.

7. ADMINISTRATION
  7.1 If any part of this policy is found to be unenforceable or invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions will continue in full force and effect. This policy constitutes the entire agreement between you and VoyagerGuard Assurance. No variation of these terms will be valid unless agreed in writing and signed by both parties.
  7.2 Throughout this policy, 'you' and 'your' refer to the policyholder named on the schedule, and 'we', 'us', and 'our' refer to VoyagerGuard Assurance. 'Trip' means the journey described in your certificate of insurance. 'Covered event' means an incident that falls within the scope of one of the categories listed in this document.

HOMEGUARD HOUSEHOLD INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by SureShield Mutual


1. DEFINITIONS AND GENERAL TERMS
  1.1 If you are dissatisfied with any aspect of our service, you should raise this in writing to our Customer Relations Team. We will investigate your complaint thoroughly and respond with a full explanation. You may also refer unresolved complaints to the Financial Ombudsman Service once our internal process is exhausted.
  1.2 We will store all personal data provided in connection with this policy in accordance with data protection law. Your information will be used solely for underwriting, claims handling, and fraud prevention purposes. We will not share your data with third parties except as required by law or with your explicit consent.
  1.3 Only the named policyholder may submit a claim under this policy. If the policyholder is unable to act, a legal representative with written authority may do so on their behalf. All communications regarding the claim must come directly from the policyholder or their authorized representative.

2. COVERAGE AND LIMITS
  2.1 The scheme covers the following categories:
  - Buildings: Covers the permanent structure of your home, including walls, roof, floors, and fixed fixtures like kitchens and bathrooms. Per-event limit: £750.
  - Contents: Covers your personal belongings inside the home, such as furniture, electronics, clothing, and valuables up to single-item limits. Per-event limit: £400.
  - Personal Liability: Covers legal costs and compensation if you accidentally injure someone or damage their property within your home. Per-event limit: £1,000.
  - Temporary Accommodation: Covers the cost of alternative housing if your home becomes uninhabitable due to an insured event. Per-event limit: £5,000.
  2.2 The deductible of £150 is subtracted from the loss before the per-event limit is applied.
  2.3 The policyholder bears no co-payment.
  2.4 Total payments in one policy year may not exceed £10,000; amounts already paid in the year reduce what remains.

  1.2 If a student believes that a decision or a procedural matter has been handled unfairly, they may submit a complaint in writing to the Endowment's internal review board. The board will assess the complaint independently and provide a reasoned response.
  1.3 A disbursement request must be made in writing, using the official form available from the Endowment's administrative office. The student must clearly state the category under which the request is made and provide all supporting documents as listed in the relevant category description.

2. COVERAGE AND LIMITS
  2.1 The scheme covers the following categories:
  - Academic Achievement: Covers a one-time recognition payment for achieving a top percentile grade point average in a given academic term. Per-event limit: €1,000.
  - Research Materials: Covers documented costs for books, software, laboratory consumables, or specialized equipment essential to a student's thesis or independent project. Per-event limit: €1,500.
  - Conference Participation: Covers registration fees and travel expenses for presenting original work at an accredited academic conference. Per-event limit: €500.
  - Community Leadership: Covers a stipend for a student who has organized a recognized volunteer initiative benefiting the local community or campus. Per-event limit: €1,000.
  2.2 The per-event limit is applied to the loss first; the deductible of €300 is then subtracted from the capped amount.
  2.3 The student bears no co-payment.
  2.4 Total payments in one policy year may not exceed €8,000; amounts already paid in the year reduce what remains.

3. EXCLUSIONS
  3.1 A disbursement request is excluded if the student has already received a payment under the same category for the same academic achievement or activity in any previous term.
  3.2 A disbursement request for a conference or research expense is excluded if the student did not actually attend the associated event or complete the associated study period.
  3.3 A disbursement request is excluded if the provider of the goods or services is a parent, sibling, spouse, or other immediate family member of the student.
  3.4 A disbursement request is excluded if the student fails to submit the required proof of payment or certificate of attendance within the defined submission window.

4. CONDITIONS
  4.1 Nothing is payable for a loss occurring fewer than 14 days after the inception date.
  4.2 A disbursement request must be notified within 7 days after the loss date; later notification is not accepted.
  4.3 Every disbursement request must be accompanied by the official receipt or certificate of attendance.

5. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURE
  Each disbursement request is assessed in this order and the first applicable step decides it: (a) waiting period (4.1), (b) notification deadline (4.2), (c) exclusions (Section 3; the lowest-numbered applicable exclusion is named), (d) documentation (4.3: the disbursement request is held, not denied), (e) amount (Section 2), (f) any amount above €2,000 requires senior-adjuster sign-off before payment.

6. PRECEDENCE
  If any other part of these terms conflicts with Section 3 or Section 5, Sections 3 and 5 prevail.
  If any provision of these rules is found to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect. The invalid provision shall be replaced with a valid one that most closely reflects the original intent.

EMPLOYEE RELOCATION ASSISTANCE POLICY
Issued by Northstar People Services


1. DEFINITIONS AND GENERAL TERMS
  1.1 For this policy, relocation means a move required by a change in the employee’s assigned work location. Household belongings means personal property ordinarily kept in the employee’s home.
  1.2 If a provision of this policy is found unenforceable, the remaining provisions continue to apply. The affected provision will be interpreted as closely as possible to its original purpose where permitted by law.
  1.3 An employee who is dissatisfied with the way a request was handled may send a written complaint to the People Services Review Team through the staff portal. The team will consider the concerns and provide a written response.

2. COVERAGE AND LIMITS
  2.1 The scheme covers the following categories:
  - Household move: Covers professional packing, transport, and delivery of the employee’s household belongings to the new residence. Per-claim limit: €5,000.
  - Relocation travel: Covers reasonable transport costs for the employee and eligible accompanying family members traveling to the new work location. Per-claim limit: €800.
  - Temporary accommodation: Covers short-term lodging while the employee arranges permanent housing near the new work location. Per-claim limit: €1,500.
  - Household storage: Covers storage of household belongings when the new residence is not ready to receive them. Per-claim limit: €250.
  2.2 The per-claim limit is applied to the loss first; the deductible of €300 is then subtracted from the capped amount.
  2.3 The employee bears 10% of the amount remaining after the deductible and limit; the provider pays the rest.
  2.4 Total payments in one policy year may not exceed €8,000; amounts already paid in the year reduce what remains.

3. EXCLUSIONS
  3.1 Personal purchases are excluded when they are not necessary to move or settle the employee’s household at the new work location.
  3.2 Ordinary commuting costs are excluded when they relate to regular travel between the employee’s residence and workplace after the relocation.
  3.3 Travel costs for guests are excluded when the travelers are not the employee or eligible accompanying family members.
  3.4 Storage costs are excluded when the employee chose storage despite the new residence being ready to receive the household belongings.

4. CONDITIONS
  4.1 Nothing is payable for a loss occurring fewer than 30 days after the inception date.
  4.2 A reimbursement request must be notified within 7 days after the loss date; later notification is not accepted.
  4.3 Every reimbursement request must be accompanied by the Itemized supplier invoice.

5. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURE
  Each reimbursement request is assessed in this order and the first applicable step decides it: (a) waiting period (4.1), (b) notification deadline (4.2), (c) exclusions (Section 3; the lowest-numbered applicable exclusion is named), (d) documentation (4.3: the reimbursement request is held, not denied), (e) amount (Section 2), (f) any amount above €1,200 requires senior-adjuster sign-off before payment.

6. PRECEDENCE
  If any other part of these terms conflicts with Section 3 or Section 5, Sections 3 and 5 prevail.
  Northstar People Services uses information in a request to administer relocation assistance, verify expenses, and maintain its records. Access is restricted to staff who need the information for those tasks, and personal information is handled under the organisation’s privacy practices.

7. ADMINISTRATION
  7.1 An employee assigned by Northstar People Services to a new work location may make a reimbursement request under this policy. The request should identify the relocation and describe the expense being submitted.
  7.2 Employees can contact the People Services Relocation Desk through the staff portal or by writing to relocation@northstar.example. The desk can explain the submission process and help identify the information needed for a request.

PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT REIMBURSEMENT POLICY
Issued by Northgate Learning Consortium


1. DEFINITIONS AND GENERAL TERMS
  1.1 All personal information gathered during the reimbursement process, including receipts, certificates, and bank details, is handled strictly in line with the organisation's data protection policy. This information is used solely to process the request, verify eligibility, and maintain financial records, and is never shared with third parties except where required by law.
  1.2 In this policy, 'training' means any structured learning activity that is directly relevant to the employee's current duties or an agreed future role within the organisation. A 'reimbursement request' is a formal application submitted by an employee to recover eligible costs they have paid personally. The 'policyholder' is the employee who has completed the training and seeks reimbursement.
  1.3 Should any part of this policy be found to be invalid or unenforceable by a competent authority, that part shall be removed, and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect. This policy replaces all previous guidance on the same subject and is effective from the date of publication.

2. COVERAGE AND LIMITS
  2.1 The scheme covers the following categories:
  - External Courses and Workshops: This covers tuition and registration fees for job-related courses, seminars, or workshops led by external institutions or trainers. Per-event limit: €250.
  - Conference and Symposium Attendance: This covers conference passes, symposium fees, and associated event registration for professional gatherings directly relevant to the employee's role. Per-event limit: €750.
  - Certification and Professional Exams: This covers costs for sitting for recognized professional certification exams and necessary re-certification assessments, including study material officially required by the certifying body. Per-event limit: €800.
  - Instructional Books and Online Resources: This covers the purchase or subscription cost of textbooks, e-books, and online learning platforms that are directly tied to a defined learning objective in the employee's development plan. Per-event limit: €400.
  2.2 The deductible of €150 is subtracted from the loss before the per-event limit is applied.
  2.3 The employee bears 20% of the amount remaining after the deductible and limit; the provider pays the rest.
  2.4 Total payments in one policy year may not exceed €12,000; amounts already paid in the year reduce what remains.

3. EXCLUSIONS
  3.1 Requests are excluded if the expense is for any durable physical item such as laptops, tablets, monitors, or desks, regardless of that item being used during training sessions.
  3.2 Requests are excluded if they include any transport, parking, meals, or lodging costs associated with attending the training event, even if those costs are part of a bundled invoice.
  3.3 Requests are excluded if the training is legally required for the employee's current position, such as health and safety, data protection, or anti-harassment certification, because those are funded by a separate departmental budget.
  3.4 Requests are excluded if the expense is for any annual or monthly membership fee for a professional association, networking group, or alumni body, even when the membership provides access to training resources.

4. CONDITIONS
  4.1 Nothing is payable for a loss occurring fewer than 14 days after the inception date.
  4.2 A reimbursement request must be notified within 7 days after the loss date; later notification is not accepted.
  4.3 Every reimbursement request must be accompanied by the itemised receipt or invoice from the training provider.

5. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURE
  Each reimbursement request is assessed in this order and the first applicable step decides it: (a) waiting period (4.1), (b) notification deadline (4.2), (c) exclusions (Section 3; the lowest-numbered applicable exclusion is named), (d) documentation (4.3: the reimbursement request is held, not denied), (e) amount (Section 2), (f) any amount above €1,200 requires senior-adjuster sign-off before payment.

6. PRECEDENCE
  If any other part of these terms conflicts with Section 3 or Section 5, Sections 3 and 5 prevail.
  Any employee on a permanent contract may submit a reimbursement request, provided that the training was undertaken during their employment and they have not previously received funding for the same activity from another source. Temporary staff and external contractors are not eligible under this scheme.

7. ADMINISTRATION
  7.1 If an employee is unhappy with any aspect of the handling of their reimbursement request, they should first raise the matter informally with the People Development Office. Should the issue remain unresolved, the employee may follow the formal internal complaint procedure, which is described in the staff handbook and on the intranet.
  7.2 To contact the scheme administrator, employees should write to the People Development Office at the Northgate Learning Consortium, either by internal mail or using the official email address published on the intranet. The administrator is available on standard working days and will respond to all queries in due course.

EMPLOYEE TRAVEL AND EXPENSE REIMBURSEMENT POLICY
Issued by Northwind Consulting Group


1. DEFINITIONS AND GENERAL TERMS
  1.1 Employees may submit a reimbursement request for expenses incurred while performing their duties. The request must be submitted through the company's expense management platform, accessible via the internal network. All requests must include the required documentation as described in the relevant section of this policy.
  1.2 If any provision of this policy is found to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect. This policy does not form part of any employee's contract of employment and may be amended by the company from time to time. The current version is always available on the intranet.
  1.3 For any questions about this policy, contact the Finance Department via the internal ticket system or by visiting the Finance office on the third floor. The Finance team is available during business hours on weekdays. The team will provide guidance on how to complete a reimbursement request and what documentation is required.

2. COVERAGE AND LIMITS
  2.1 The scheme covers the following categories:
  - Transportation: Covers public transit, taxi, rideshare, and rental car costs incurred while traveling on approved company business. Per-claim limit: €5,000.
  - Lodging: Covers hotel, motel, or short-term apartment accommodation expenses during business travel away from the employee's home location. Per-claim limit: €500.
  - Meals and Incidentals: Covers reasonable meal expenses and incidental costs directly related to business travel, such as tips, baggage handling, and internet fees. Per-claim limit: €3,000.
  - Conference and Training: Covers registration fees and related materials for conferences, seminars, or professional development courses required for the employee's role. Per-claim limit: €400.
  2.2 The per-claim limit is applied to the loss first; the deductible of €300 is then subtracted from the capped amount.
  2.3 The employee bears 25% of the amount remaining after the deductible and limit; the provider pays the rest.
  2.4 Total payments in one policy year may not exceed €12,000; amounts already paid in the year reduce what remains.

3. EXCLUSIONS
  3.1 Costs for alcoholic beverages, minibar items, or luxury hotel rooms are excluded from reimbursement when the expense is not directly tied to a mandatory business function.
  3.2 Expenses incurred for personal sightseeing, entertainment, or non-business detours taken during a business trip are excluded when the trip's primary purpose was not the company's business objective.
  3.3 Reimbursement for cash, personal property, or company property that is lost, stolen, or damaged while in the employee's possession is excluded unless a police report is filed.
  3.4 Normal commuting expenses between the employee's home and their regular work location are excluded, as these are considered personal costs, not business travel.

4. CONDITIONS
  4.1 Nothing is payable for a loss occurring fewer than 7 days after the inception date.
  4.2 A reimbursement request must be notified within 14 days after the loss date; later notification is not accepted.
  4.3 Every reimbursement request must be accompanied by the detailed invoice or receipt.

5. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURE
  Each reimbursement request is assessed in this order and the first applicable step decides it: (a) waiting period (4.1), (b) notification deadline (4.2), (c) exclusions (Section 3; the lowest-numbered applicable exclusion is named), (d) documentation (4.3: the reimbursement request is held, not denied), (e) amount (Section 2), (f) any amount above €800 requires senior-adjuster sign-off before payment.

6. PRECEDENCE
  If any other part of these terms conflicts with Section 3 or Section 5, Sections 3 and 5 prevail.
  This policy applies to all employees of Northwind Consulting Group who incur travel or business expenses on behalf of the company. For the purpose of this policy, an 'employee' includes any person on the payroll, including temporary and part-time staff. The policy is designed to ensure consistent and fair treatment of all staff and to comply with applicable tax regulations.

7. ADMINISTRATION
  7.1 Employees who believe that a reimbursement request has not been handled fairly or who have concerns about this policy may raise the matter with their line manager or the People Operations team. The company aims to resolve any such concerns promptly and courteously. No employee will be disadvantaged for raising a concern in good faith.
  7.2 Data provided in reimbursement requests, including travel itineraries and receipts, is stored in protected electronic systems. Access to this data is restricted to Finance and Human Resources staff for verification and audit purposes. The company processes personal data in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation and the internal Data Protection Manual.

  4.1 Nothing is payable for a loss occurring fewer than 7 days after the inception date.
  4.2 A reimbursement request must be notified within 21 days after the loss date; later notification is not accepted.
  4.3 Every reimbursement request must be accompanied by the police report.

6. PRECEDENCE
  If any other part of these terms conflicts with Section 3 or Section 5, Sections 3 and 5 prevail.

Data will not be shared with third parties except as required for fraud prevention or legal compliance. The renter has the right to access and rectify any inaccurate personal data held by the provider.

7. ADMINISTRATION
  7.1 If any part of this waiver is found to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect. The invalidity of one clause does not affect the validity of the other clauses. This waiver is governed by the laws of the jurisdiction in which the rental office is located, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
  7.2 If the renter is dissatisfied with any decision regarding this waiver, they may file a complaint with the provider's internal complaints office. The complaint should include the rental number, a description of the issue, and copies of relevant documents. The provider will review the complaint and provide a written response, detailing any further steps available within the organization.

state.policy_document:
EMPLOYEE RELOCATION ASSISTANCE POLICY
Issued by Northstar People Services


1. DEFINITIONS AND GENERAL TERMS
  1.1 For this policy, relocation means a move required by a change in the employee’s assigned work location. Household belongings means personal property ordinarily kept in the employee’s home.
  1.2 An employee who is dissatisfied with the way a request was handled may send a written complaint to the People Services Review Team through the staff portal. The team will consider the concerns and provide a written response.
  1.3 Employees can contact the People Services Relocation Desk through the staff portal or by writing to relocation@northstar.example. The desk can explain the submission process and help identify the information needed for a request.

2. COVERAGE AND LIMITS
  2.1 The scheme covers the following categories:
  - Household move: Covers professional packing, transport, and delivery of the employee’s household belongings to the new residence. Per-claim limit: €500.
  - Relocation travel: Covers reasonable transport costs for the employee and eligible accompanying family members traveling to the new work location. Per-claim limit: €3,000.
  - Temporary accommodation: Covers short-term lodging while the employee arranges permanent housing near the new work location. Per-claim limit: €1,000.
  - Household storage: Covers storage of household belongings when the new residence is not ready to receive them. Per-claim limit: €3,000.
  2.2 The per-claim limit is applied to the loss first; the deductible of €150 is then subtracted from the capped amount.
  2.3 The employee bears 25% of the amount remaining after the deductible and limit; the provider pays the rest.
  2.4 Total payments in one policy year may not exceed €5,000; amounts already paid in the year reduce what remains.

3. EXCLUSIONS
  3.1 Personal purchases are excluded when they are not necessary to move or settle the employee’s household at the new work location.
  3.2 Ordinary commuting costs are excluded when they relate to regular travel between the employee’s residence and workplace after the relocation.
  3.3 Travel costs for guests are excluded when the travelers are not the employee or eligible accompanying family members.
  3.4 Storage costs are excluded when the employee chose storage despite the new residence being ready to receive the household belongings.

4. CONDITIONS
  4.1 Nothing is payable for a loss occurring fewer than 30 days after the inception date.
  4.2 A reimbursement request must be notified within 30 days after the loss date; later notification is not accepted.
  4.3 Every reimbursement request must be accompanied by the Itemized supplier invoice.

5. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURE
  Each reimbursement request is assessed in this order and the first applicable step decides it: (a) waiting period (4.1), (b) notification deadline (4.2), (c) exclusions (Section 3; the lowest-numbered applicable exclusion is named), (d) documentation (4.3: the reimbursement request is held, not denied), (e) amount (Section 2), (f) any amount above €1,200 requires senior-adjuster sign-off before payment.

6. PRECEDENCE
  If any other part of these terms conflicts with Section 3 or Section 5, Sections 3 and 5 prevail.
  Northstar People Services uses information in a request to administer relocation assistance, verify expenses, and maintain its records. Access is restricted to staff who need the information for those tasks, and personal information is handled under the organisation’s privacy practices.

7. ADMINISTRATION
  7.1 If a provision of this policy is found unenforceable, the remaining provisions continue to apply. The affected provision will be interpreted as closely as possible to its original purpose where permitted by law.
  7.2 An employee assigned by Northstar People Services to a new work location may make a reimbursement request under this policy. The request should identify the relocation and describe the expense being submitted.

policy.title: Financial Controls and Expense Approval Policy
policy.organisation: Northstar Tidal Analytics, a fictional marine forecasting company
policy.purpose: This policy establishes how Northstar Tidal Analytics authorises, records, and reviews expenses. It protects company funds and supports accurate financial reporting and timely escalation of control failures.

section_1_impact_classes.A: Class A means no harm occurred and no financial or sensitive information was exposed.
section_1_impact_classes.B: Class B means exposure was limited to internal staff or the harm was minor.
section_1_impact_classes.C: Class C means significant exposure occurred or a customer, colleague, or the organisation suffered significant harm.
section_1_impact_classes.D: Class D means serious harm occurred, the organisation faces legal liability, or the event must be reported to a regulator.

section_2_severity_calculation: Start at the base level of the impact class: Class A = 0, Class B = 1, Class C = 2, Class D = 3.
Subtract 1 level if the employee reported the matter themselves within 24 hours and the act was not deliberate.
Add 1 level if the act was deliberate (the employee knew the rule and chose to break it).
Add 1 level if the employee has a substantiated violation of the same policy in the previous 12 months.
The final level is limited to the range 0-3. Adjustments are applied together; a deliberate act never receives the self-report reduction.

section_3_levels.0: Level Zero — Coaching and a documented reminder
section_3_levels.1: Level One — Written warning and required controls training
section_3_levels.2: Level Two — Final warning and temporary removal of approval authority
section_3_levels.3: Level Three — Dismissal and referral to legal or regulatory authorities where required

section_1_impact_classes.A: Clase A: No ocurrió ningún daño y la acción u omisión no generó exposición a riesgos ni escrutinio regulatorio.
section_1_impact_classes.B: Clase B: La acción u omisión generó una exposición interna limitada, como un error administrativo menor o una breve demora operativa, sin daño a ninguna persona ni propiedad.
section_1_impact_classes.C: Clase C: La acción u omisión provocó una exposición o un daño significativo a un cliente, un colega o la organización, como un plazo de entrega incumplido, daños al vehículo o un incidente a punto de ocurrir.
section_1_impact_classes.D: Clase D: La acción u omisión resultó en un daño grave, responsabilidad legal o un evento que debe reportarse al regulador, como un accidente con lesiones, un registro falsificado o una infracción de horas de conducción que desencadena una auditoría de cumplimiento.

section_2_severity_calculation: Comience en el nivel base de la clase de impacto: Clase A = 0, Clase B = 1, Clase C = 2, Clase D = 3.
Sume 1 nivel si el empleado tiene una infracción comprobada de la misma política en los 12 meses anteriores.
Reste 1 nivel si el empleado informó el asunto por cuenta propia dentro de las 24 horas y el acto no fue deliberado.
Sume 1 nivel si el acto fue deliberado (el empleado conocía la regla y decidió infringirla).
El nivel final se limita al rango de 0-3. Los ajustes se aplican en conjunto; un acto deliberado nunca recibe la reducción por informar el asunto por cuenta propia.

section_3_levels.0: Nivel 0: Aclaración verbal y nota en el expediente por descuidos administrativos menores, sin más acciones.
section_3_levels.1: Nivel 1: Advertencia por escrito y finalización obligatoria de un módulo de actualización sobre horas de conducción o revisiones del vehículo.
section_3_levels.2: Nivel 2: Última advertencia por escrito, suspensión de las funciones de conducción durante una semana y una revisión completa del historial de cumplimiento del conductor.
section_3_levels.3: Nivel 3: Terminación de la relación laboral y, cuando corresponda, remisión a la autoridad de transporte pertinente para la acción sobre la licencia o para otros procedimientos legales.

incident_report.summary: Un conductor registró deliberadamente horas de conducción falsas para ocultar un exceso de trabajo, lo cual salió a la luz tras un incidente relacionado con la fatiga en la autopista; se notificó a la policía y a la autoridad de transporte, y la empresa recibió una notificación formal de sanción.
investigator_findings: El investigador no encontró indicios de que el empleado supiera que estaba infringiendo la regla.
No se ha confirmado que el empleado haya infringido esta política en los últimos 12 meses.
Un colega planteó el asunto diez días después.

policy.title: Juniper Hearth Food Safety and Kitchen Compliance Policy
policy.organisation: Juniper Hearth Kitchens, a neighborhood restaurant group
policy.purpose: This policy sets clear food safety practices for everyone working in Juniper Hearth Kitchens. It supports safe food handling, protects guests and colleagues, and guides consistent responses to kitchen incidents.

section_1_impact_classes.A: Class A means a food safety deviation caused no harm and no exposure because it was corrected before food or a person could be affected.
section_1_impact_classes.B: Class B means a deviation caused limited internal exposure or minor harm to a colleague, without significant customer impact.
section_1_impact_classes.C: Class C means a deviation caused significant exposure or harm to a customer or colleague, or significant harm to the organisation.
section_1_impact_classes.D: Class D means an incident caused serious harm, created legal liability, or met the threshold for reporting to a regulator.

section_2_severity_calculation: Start at the base level of the impact class: Class A = 0, Class B = 1, Class C = 2, Class D = 3.
Add 1 level if the employee has a substantiated violation of the same policy in the previous 12 months.
Add 1 level if the act was deliberate (the employee knew the rule and chose to break it).
Subtract 1 level if the employee reported the matter themselves within 24 hours and the act was not deliberate.
The final level is limited to the range 0-3. Adjustments are applied together; a deliberate act never receives the self-report reduction.

section_3_levels.1: Level One — written warning and refresher training
section_3_levels.2: Level Two — final warning and temporary removal from food handling
section_3_levels.3: Level Three — suspension or termination, with regulator notification when required

incident_report.summary: An employee set a sealed container of raw poultry on a clean prep counter. The employee moved the sealed container to cold storage before the counter was used, and no food or person was exposed.
investigator_findings: The employee says they did not realise this was against the rule.
The employee has had no substantiated violations of this policy in the last 12 months.

policy.title: سياسة سلامة الغذاء والامتثال في مطبخ Juniper Hearth
policy.organisation: Juniper Hearth Kitchens، مجموعة مطاعم في الحي
policy.purpose: تضع هذه السياسة ممارسات واضحة لسلامة الغذاء لكل من يعمل في Juniper Hearth Kitchens. وهي تدعم التعامل الآمن مع الأغذية، وتحمي الضيوف والزملاء، وتوجّه الاستجابات المتسقة لحوادث المطبخ.

section_1_impact_classes.A: الفئة A تعني أن انحرافًا في سلامة الغذاء لم يسبب ضررًا ولا تعريضًا للخطر لأنه صُحِّح قبل أن يتأثر الطعام أو أي شخص.
section_1_impact_classes.B: الفئة B تعني أن انحرافًا تسبب في تعريض داخلي محدود للخطر أو ضرر طفيف لزميل، دون أثر كبير على العملاء.
section_1_impact_classes.C: الفئة C تعني أن انحرافًا تسبب في تعريض كبير للخطر أو ضرر لعميل أو زميل، أو ضرر كبير للمؤسسة.
section_1_impact_classes.D: الفئة D تعني أن حادثًا تسبب في ضرر جسيم أو أوجد مسؤولية قانونية أو بلغ حد الإبلاغ إلى جهة تنظيمية.

section_2_severity_calculation: ابدأ بالمستوى الأساسي لفئة الأثر: الفئة A = 0، الفئة B = 1، الفئة C = 2، الفئة D = 3.
أضف مستوى واحدًا (1) إذا كانت لدى الموظف مخالفة مثبتة لنفس السياسة خلال الأشهر الـ12 السابقة.
ارفع المستوى بمقدار 1 إذا كان الفعل متعمدًا (كان الموظف يعلم بالقاعدة واختار مخالفتها).
اطرح مستوى واحدًا (1) إذا أبلغ الموظف عن الأمر بنفسه خلال 24 ساعة ولم يكن الفعل متعمدًا.
يُحصر المستوى النهائي في النطاق 0-3. تُطبق التعديلات معًا؛ ولا يحصل الفعل المتعمد أبدًا على خفض الإبلاغ الذاتي.

section_3_levels.1: المستوى واحد — إنذار كتابي وتدريب تنشيطي
section_3_levels.2: المستوى اثنان — إنذار نهائي وإبعاد مؤقت عن التعامل مع الأغذية
section_3_levels.3: المستوى ثلاثة — إيقاف أو إنهاء الخدمة، مع إخطار الجهة التنظيمية عند الاقتضاء

policy.title: Safe Plate Protocol for Kitchen Operations
policy.organisation: Harbourlight Catering Collective, a mid-sized event catering company
policy.purpose: This policy defines the standards for food handling, storage, and preparation to prevent contamination and foodborne illness. It also establishes a classification system for incidents to guide corrective actions and training priorities.

section_1_impact_classes.A: Class A: No harm occurred and no food or surface was exposed to a potential contaminant beyond standard kitchen practices.
section_1_impact_classes.B: Class B: Limited internal exposure occurred, such as a minor spill or brief temperature deviation that was corrected without affecting served food or causing harm.
section_1_impact_classes.C: Class C: Significant exposure or harm affected a customer, colleague, or the organisation, such as serving food past its safe hold time or causing a mild allergic reaction.
section_1_impact_classes.D: Class D: Serious harm, legal liability, or a regulator-reportable event occurred, such as a hospitalisation from food poisoning or a confirmed pest infestation in a storage area.

section_2_severity_calculation: Start at the base level of the impact class: Class A = 0, Class B = 1, Class C = 2, Class D = 3.
Add 1 level if the act was deliberate (the employee knew the rule and chose to break it).
Add 1 level if the employee has a substantiated violation of the same policy in the previous 12 months.
Subtract 1 level if the employee reported the matter themselves within 24 hours and the act was not deliberate.
The final level is limited to the range 0-3. Adjustments are applied together; a deliberate act never receives the self-report reduction.

section_3_levels.0: Level 0: Verbal reminder and a note on file for the individual involved.
section_3_levels.1: Level 1: Written warning and mandatory retraining on the specific procedure within seven days.
section_3_levels.2: Level 2: Suspension from kitchen duties for two shifts and a formal performance review.
section_3_levels.3: Level 3: Termination of employment and potential referral to relevant regulatory bodies if required by law.

incident_report.summary: An employee used a cleaning chemical to wipe a counter where bread dough was rising, without rinsing the surface afterwards. The resulting bread was served at a charity event, and one elderly guest suffered severe chemical burns to the mouth requiring emergency care; the regulator was informed.
investigator_findings: The matter came to light during a routine audit.
The employee says they did not realise this was against the rule.
The employee has had no substantiated violations of this policy in the last 12 months.

questions.instructions: Under the policy, which severity level applies to this incident?

criteria.A: Level 0: Level 0: Verbal reminder and a note on file for the individual involved.
criteria.B: Level 1: Level 1: Written warning and mandatory retraining on the specific procedure within seven days.
criteria.C: Level 2: Level 2: Suspension from kitchen duties for two shifts and a formal performance review.
criteria.D: Level 3: Level 3: Termination of employment and potential referral to relevant regulatory bodies if required by law.

policy.title: Protocolo Prato Seguro para Operações de Cozinha
policy.organisation: Harbourlight Catering Collective, uma empresa de buffet para eventos de médio porte
policy.purpose: Esta política define os padrões de manuseio, armazenamento e preparo de alimentos para evitar contaminação e doenças transmitidas por alimentos. Também estabelece um sistema de classificação de incidentes para orientar ações corretivas e prioridades de treinamento.

section_1_impact_classes.A: Classe A: Não houve dano e nenhum alimento ou superfície foi exposto a um contaminante potencial além das práticas normais de cozinha.
section_1_impact_classes.B: Classe B: Ocorreu exposição interna limitada, como um pequeno derramamento ou um breve desvio de temperatura corrigido sem afetar os alimentos servidos nem causar dano.
section_1_impact_classes.C: Classe C: Exposição ou dano significativo afetou um cliente, colega ou a organização, como servir alimentos além do tempo seguro de conservação ou causar uma reação alérgica leve.
section_1_impact_classes.D: Classe D: Ocorreu dano grave, responsabilidade legal ou um evento que deve ser comunicado ao órgão regulador, como uma hospitalização por intoxicação alimentar ou uma infestação de pragas confirmada em uma área de armazenamento.

section_2_severity_calculation: Comece no nível-base da classe de impacto: Classe A = 0, Classe B = 1, Classe C = 2, Classe D = 3.
Adicione 1 nível se o ato foi deliberado (o funcionário conhecia a regra e escolheu descumpri-la).
Adicione 1 nível se houver uma violação comprovada da mesma política pelo funcionário nos 12 meses anteriores.
Subtraia 1 nível se o próprio funcionário comunicou o ocorrido em até 24 horas e o ato não foi deliberado.
O nível final é limitado ao intervalo de 0-3. Os ajustes são aplicados em conjunto; um ato deliberado nunca recebe a redução por comunicação espontânea.

section_3_levels.0: Nível 0: Lembrete verbal e uma anotação no registro da pessoa envolvida.
section_3_levels.1: Nível 1: Advertência por escrito e retreinamento obrigatório no procedimento específico em até sete dias.
section_3_levels.2: Nível 2: Afastamento das tarefas de cozinha por dois turnos e uma avaliação formal de desempenho.
section_3_levels.3: Nível 3: Rescisão do contrato de trabalho e possível encaminhamento aos órgãos reguladores competentes, se exigido por lei.

incident_report.summary: Um funcionário usou um produto químico de limpeza para limpar uma bancada onde a massa de pão estava crescendo, sem enxaguar a superfície depois. O pão resultante foi servido em um evento beneficente, e um convidado idoso sofreu queimaduras químicas graves na boca que exigiram atendimento de emergência; o órgão regulador foi informado.
investigator_findings: O ocorrido veio à tona durante uma auditoria de rotina.
O funcionário afirma que não percebeu que isso era contra a regra.
O funcionário não teve nenhuma violação comprovada desta política nos últimos 12 meses.

questions.instructions: De acordo com a política, qual nível de gravidade se aplica a este incidente?

criteria.A: Nível 0: Nível 0: Lembrete verbal e uma anotação no registro da pessoa envolvida.

criteria.D: Nível 3: Nível 3: Rescisão do contrato de trabalho e possível encaminhamento aos órgãos reguladores competentes, se exigido por lei.

policy.title: Политика поведения и уважительного отношения на рабочем месте
policy.organisation: Northstar Tidal Research, консалтинговая компания в области морских наук
policy.purpose: Настоящая политика устанавливает требования к уважительному, безопасному и профессиональному поведению в Northstar Tidal Research. Она предусматривает единый порядок оценки инцидентов, связанных с поведением, и применения соразмерных последствий.

section_1_impact_classes.A: Класс A означает, что поведение не причинило вреда и не подвергло риску какую-либо информацию или человека.
section_1_impact_classes.B: Класс B означает, что поведение причинило незначительный вред или привело к ограниченному раскрытию информации внутри организации.
section_1_impact_classes.C: Класс C означает, что поведение привело к значительному раскрытию информации или причинило вред клиенту, коллеге либо организации.
section_1_impact_classes.D: Класс D означает, что поведение причинило серьезный вред, повлекло юридическую ответственность или привело к событию, о котором необходимо сообщить регулирующему органу.

section_2_severity_calculation: Начните с базового уровня класса воздействия: Класс A = 0, Класс B = 1, Класс C = 2, Класс D = 3.
Добавьте 1 уровень, если за предыдущие 12 месяцев было подтверждено нарушение сотрудником той же политики.
Понизьте уровень на 1, если сотрудник сам сообщил о случившемся в течение 24 часов и действие не было преднамеренным.
Добавьте 1 уровень, если действие было преднамеренным (сотрудник знал правило и решил его нарушить).
Итоговый уровень ограничен диапазоном 0-3. Корректировки применяются вместе; за преднамеренное действие никогда не применяется снижение за самостоятельное сообщение.

section_3_levels.2: Уровень два — последнее предупреждение и обучение правилам поведения
section_3_levels.3: Уровень три — отстранение от работы или увольнение

Сотрудник говорит, что не понимал, что это противоречит правилу.

policy.title: 職場での行動と敬意に関するポリシー
policy.organisation: Northstar Tidal Research、海洋科学コンサルティング会社
policy.purpose: このポリシーは、Northstar Tidal Research における敬意ある、安全で、プロフェッショナルな行動への期待を定めます。行動に関する事案を評価し、適切な結果を適用するための一貫した方法を提供します。

section_1_impact_classes.A: クラスAは、その行動が害を及ぼさず、情報や人をリスクにさらさなかったことを意味します。
section_1_impact_classes.B: クラスBは、その行動が軽微な害、または組織内での限定的な露出を引き起こしたことを意味します。
section_1_impact_classes.C: クラスCは、その行動が顧客、同僚、または組織に重大な露出または害を引き起こしたことを意味します。
section_1_impact_classes.D: クラスDは、その行動が重大な害や法的責任を引き起こした、または規制当局に報告しなければならない事象であったことを意味します。

section_2_severity_calculation: 影響クラスの基本レベルから開始します：クラスA = 0、クラスB = 1、クラスC = 2、クラスD = 3。
従業員に過去12か月以内に同じポリシーへの違反が立証されている場合、レベルを1加算します。
従業員が24時間以内に自らその件を報告し、かつ行為が故意でなかった場合、レベルを1つ減算します。
行為が故意であった場合（従業員が規則を知りながら違反することを選んだ場合）、レベルを1つ上げます。

# Conventional Commit Policy for Embedded Firmware (v4.2)

## 1. Allowed Types
The commit type MUST be one of: `feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `perf`, `security`.

## 2. Scope Rules
The scope (text in parentheses) MUST match the root directory of at least one changed file path. If files are changed in multiple root directories, the scope must be `core` or `all`.

## 3. Subject Line Constraints
- Must be imperative mood (e.g., "add", not "added").
- Maximum length: 50 characters (including type and scope).
- No trailing punctuation.

## 4. Body & Footers
- Body is optional.
- If the body contains the phrase "BREAKING CHANGE", a footer `BREAKING CHANGE: <description>` is MANDATORY.
- If the type is `security`, a footer `Refs: <ticket-id>` is MANDATORY.

## 5. Evaluation Order
Checks are performed in this exact order. The first failure determines the rejection reason:
1. `bad_type`: Type not in allowed list OR type implies a domain (e.g., `security`) that contradicts the file paths (e.g., no security-related files changed).
2. `scope_mismatch`: Scope does not match any changed file root.
3. `subject_too_long`: Subject > 50 chars.
4. `not_imperative`: Subject verb is not imperative.
5. `missing_footer`: Required footer absent based on body content or type.

---

SECTION 7: ENTITY COMPONENT SYSTEM (ECS) QUERY RETURNS

7.1 General Rule:
All functions returning a collection of entities (List<Entity>) must adhere to the
'Empty Collection' pattern. If no entities match the query criteria, the function
MUST return an empty list (`new List<Entity>()`).

7.2 Prohibited Patterns:
- Returning `null` (or `None` in Python bindings) is strictly forbidden for 
  collection returns. This prevents NullReferenceExceptions in the update loop.
- Returning `undefined` is forbidden.

7.3 Exceptions:
- Functions annotated with `[Obsolete]` or `# @deprecated` may return `null` to 
  signal end-of-life behavior.
- Functions explicitly documented with "Returns null if no entities found" are 
  exempt from 7.1.

7.4 Precedence:
If a function's individual docstring conflicts with this global standard, the 
global standard (Section 7.1) takes precedence UNLESS the function is marked deprecated.

    Parameters:

    Returns:
        list: A list of active particle entities. 
        (Note: Implementation detail - returns None if group is empty to skip loop)

    active = []

Subject: Likelihood of Severe Corrosion (SC) Event in Reactor Sites

1. Scope
This report assesses the likelihood of an SC event (defined as material loss > 2mm/year) in our new Reactor Site Y over a 1-year period. Site Y has 10 identical reactor units.

2. Precedent Data: Industry-Wide SC Incidents
Table 1: Annual SC Incidents in Chemical Industry (2015-2023)
Year | Total Industry Sites | Total SC Incidents
2015 | 1200 | 18
2016 | 1250 | 15
2017 | 1300 | 22
2018 | 1280 | 12
2019 | 1350 | 25
2020 | 1300 | 10
2021 | 1400 | 28
2022 | 1450 | 20
2023 | 1500 | 15

3. Footnotes & Definitions
(a) 'Total Industry Sites' refers to the number of active chemical processing plants in the global registry. Each plant may contain multiple reactor units.
(b) 'SC Incident' is defined at the *site* level in the industry registry. If multiple reactors in one site experience SC, it is counted as 1 site incident.
(c) Our Site Y is a single site containing 10 reactor units. The industry data does not distinguish between single-unit and multi-unit sites.
(d) For the purpose of this assessment, assume that the probability of an SC event in a site is independent of the number of reactors within that site, but the rate must be scaled from the industry-wide site-level incidence to our specific site context. However, per company policy (Section 4.2), when scaling from site-level industry data to a specific site with a known number of units, the annual probability for the specific site is calculated as: (Total SC Incidents / Total Industry Sites) * (Number of Units in Site Y / Average Units per Industry Site). Assume the average industry site has 20 reactor units.

1: Rare (<1 in 100 yrs)
2: Unlikely (1 in 20-100)
3: Possible (1 in 5-20)
4: Likely (1 in 2-5)
5: Almost certain (>1 in 2)

Sponsor: Democratic senator from CT
Official title: A bill to increase accessibility to the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System, to facilitate data sharing between such system and the National Crime Information Center database of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and for other purposes.
Short title: Billy's Law or the Help Find the Missing Act
Summary of the bill as introduced (Congressional Research Service): This bill provides statutory authority for the Department of Justice (DOJ) to maintain the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System (NamUs) consistent with its existing purpose and structure. NamUs is a national information clearinghouse and resource center for cases involving missing persons and unidentified or unclaimed remains. NamUs is administered by the National Institute of Justice within DOJ. The bill also establishes new requirements. First, it requires a law enforcement agency that submits a missing child report to the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) to also submit the missing child report to NamUs. The NCIC is a computerized index of criminal justice data and files for reports of missing and unidentified persons. Current law requires law enforcement agencies to submit missing child reports to the NCIC database but not to the NamUs databases. Ethereum improvement proposal (Standards Track, Core, created 2015-11-22)
Title: Gas Usage for RETURN and CALL
Abstract: This EIP makes it possible to call functions that return strings and other dynamically-sized arrays. Currently, when another contract / function is called from inside the Ethereum Virtual Machine, the size of the output has to be specified in advance. It is of course possible to give a larger size, but gas also has to be paid for memory that is not written to, which makes returning dynamically-sized data both costly and inflexible to the extent that it is actually unusable. The solution proposed in this EIP is to charge gas only for memory that is actually written to at the time the CALL returns.

Ethereum improvement proposal (Standards Track, Core, created 2021-03-06)
Title: Paged memory allocation for the EVM
Abstract: Presently, the EVM charges for memory as a linear array starting at address 0 and extending to the highest address that has been read from or written to. This suffices for simple uses, but means that compilers have to generate programs that use memory compactly, which leads to wasted gas with reallocation of memory elements, and makes some memory models such as separate heap and stack areas impractical. This EIP proposes changing to a page-based billing model, which adds minimal complexity to implementations, while providing for much more versatility in EVM programs.

Ethereum improvement proposal (Standards Track, Networking, created 2019-05-03)
Title: Fork identifier for chain compatibility checks
Abstract: There are many public and private Ethereum networks, but the discovery protocol doesn't differentiate between them. The only way to check if a peer is good or bad (same chain or not), is to establish a TCP/IP connection, wrap it with RLPx cryptography, then execute an eth handshake. This is an extreme cost to bear if it turns out that the remote peer is on a different network and it's not even precise enough to differentiate Ethereum and Ethereum Classic. This cost is magnified for small networks, where a lot more trial and errors are needed to find good nodes. Even if the peer is on the same chain, during non-controversial consensus upgrades, not everybody updates their nodes in time (developer nodes, leftovers, etc). These stale nodes put a meaningless burden on the peer-to-peer network, since they just latch on to good nodes, but don't accept upgraded blocks.

Ethereum improvement proposal (Standards Track, ERC, created 2018-09-25)
Title: RTA-Controlled Security Token
Description: Security tokens where the Registered Transfer Agent has exclusive control over transfers for regulatory compliance
Abstract: ERC-1450 facilitates the recording of ownership and transfer of securities sold in compliance with Securities Act Regulations CF, D, and A. This standard is informed by practical operational experience from SEC-registered transfer agents, broker-dealers, and alternative trading systems that have collectively managed billions in compliant securities offerings. The design addresses the full lifecycle of digital securities from issuance through secondary trading. The standard introduces a unique RTA-controlled model where the Registered Transfer Agent maintains exclusive authority over all token operations. Unlike permissionless tokens, ERC-1450 enforces strict compliance by requiring the RTA to execute all mints, burns, and transfers, while disabling direct value movement via transfer() and approve().
Requires: EIP-20, EIP-165, EIP-6093

Ethereum improvement proposal (Standards Track, ERC, created 2023-07-26)
Title: Parent-Governed Non-Fungible Tokens Nesting
Description: An interface for Non-Fungible Tokens Nesting with emphasis on parent token's control over the relationship.
Abstract: ❗️ The Parent-Governed NFT Nesting standard extends ERC-721 by allowing for a new inter-NFT relationship and interaction. At its core, the idea behind the proposal is simple: the owner of an NFT does not have to be an Externally Owned Account (EOA) or a smart contract, it can also be an NFT. The process of nesting an NFT into another is functionally identical to sending it to another user. The process of sending a token out of another one involves issuing a transaction from the account owning the parent token. An NFT can be owned by a single other NFT, but can in turn have a number of NFTs that it owns. This proposal establishes the framework for the parent-child relationships of NFTs. A parent token is the one that owns another token. A child token is a token that is owned by another token. A token can be both a parent and child at the same time.
Requires: EIP-165, EIP-721

Abstract: A transparent contract is a proxy contract design pattern that provides the following: 1. A way to add, replace and remove multiple functions of a contract atomically (at the same time). 1. Standard events to show what functions are added, replaced and removed from a contract, and why the changes are made. 2. A standard way to query a contract to discover and retrieve information about all functions exposed by it. 3. Solves the 24KB maximum contract size limitation, making the maximum contract size of a transparent contract practically unlimited. This standard makes the worry about contract size a thing of the past. 4. Enables an upgradeable contract to become immutable in the future if desired.

Summary: Werkzeug safe_join() allows Windows special device names with compound extensions
Details: Werkzeug's `safe_join` function allows path segments with Windows device names that have file extensions or trailing spaces. On Windows, there are special device names such as `CON`, `AUX`, etc that are implicitly present and readable in every directory. Windows still accepts them with any file extension, such as `CON.txt`, or trailing spaces such as `CON `. This was previously reported as but the fix failed to account for compound extensions such as `CON.txt.html` or trailing spaces. It also missed some additional special names. `send_from_directory` uses `safe_join` to safely serve files at user-specified paths under a directory. If the application is running on Windows, and the requested path ends with a special device name, the file will be opened successfully, but reading will hang indefinitely.

The expression can contain arbitrary Clojure or Python code. The attacker must know a valid project ID of a project that contains at least one row. The `com.google.refine.commands.expr.PreviewExpressionCommand` class contains the following comment: However, this appears to be false (or no longer true). The expression being previewed (executed) can be written in GREL, Python, or Clojure. Since there are no restrictions on what code can be executed, the expression can do anything the user running OpenRefine can do. For instance, the following expressions start a calculator: The lack of restrictions on expressions is arguably not a problem if the user is typing their own expressions into OpenRefine: they could have just as well typed them into Clojure or Python directly.

Self-hosters are impacted if running Ghost a version between v4.46.0 and v4.48.7 or any version of v5 prior to v5.22.7. Details: `read_skill_file()` in `skill_tools.py` allows reading arbitrary files from the filesystem by accepting an unrestricted `skill_path` parameter. An agent influenced by prompt injection can exfiltrate sensitive files without triggering any approval prompt. The vulnerability is a missing authorization check in `read_skill_file()` at `src/praisonai-agents/praisonaiagents/tools/skill_tools.py:128`. The function's path validation on line 163 only ensures `file_path` doesn't escape `skill_path` via directory traversal: The check on line 163 prevents `file_path` from containing `../` to escape `skill_path`, but `skill_path` itself is completely unrestricted — it can be any absolute directory on the filesystem. `read_skill_file` has neither workspace confinement nor an approval gate. It is also not listed in `DEFAULT_DANGEROUS_TOOLS` (registry.py:31-46), so no approval is ever requested.

Details: A vulnerability in Nuclei's DAST template loading path allows unsigned `code:` protocol templates to execute, bypassing the cryptographic signature requirement that is meant to prevent arbitrary command execution from untrusted templates. The issue is in the template loader's DAST loading branch. When `-dast` is enabled and a template contains a `fuzzing:` block, the loader accepted the template through a code path that omitted the unsigned-code-template signature check present in the normal loading branch. Nuclei requires `code:` protocol templates to be cryptographically signed before execution. Unsigned code templates are normally skipped with a warning. However, when a template combined a `fuzzing:` block (making it DAST-eligible) with an unsigned `code:` block, enabling `-dast` routed the template through the DAST loader branch, which did not enforce signature verification.

These values were then returned to the attacker when the page was reopened. Exfiltration of sensitive environment variables (APP_KEY, DB credentials, AWS keys, etc.). Could enable further attacks: database access, cookie forgery, AWS resource access. Requires authenticated backend access with Editor permissions. Only relevant when `cms.safe_mode` is enabled (otherwise direct PHP injection is already possible). The vulnerability has been patched in v3.7.14 and v4.1.10. Summary: mediasoup: SCTP state cookie lacks cryptographic authentication, enabling unauthorized association establishment (RFC 9260 violation)
Details: mediasoup's built-in SCTP stack (introduced in v3.20.0) authenticates SCTP state cookies using only hardcoded magic byte sequences rather than a per-instance HMAC keyed with a secret, violating RFC 9260 Section 5.1.3. An on-path attacker targeting a PlainTransport with SCTP enabled (and no SRTP/DTLS protection) can craft a forged COOKIE-ECHO chunk that passes all validation, establishing an unauthorized SCTP association and gaining the ability to inject DataChannel messages as a trusted peer. RFC 9260 Section 5.1.3 states: "An endpoint MUST use a one-time-use secret key to protect the State Cookie." The mediasoup implementation ignores this requirement. The state cookie is defined in `worker/include/RTC/SCTP/association/StateCookie.hpp` with the following structure (44 bytes total): Offset 0: Magic1 = `"msworker"` (hardcoded, 8 bytes). Offset 8: localVerificationTag (4 bytes, attacker-controlled). Offset 12: remoteVerificationTag (4 bytes, attacker-controlled).

Title: Reynolds Stress Budget Analysis of DNS Data for Flow over a Gaussian Bump
Abstract: Reynolds stress budgets computed from a direct numerical simulation of the spanwise-periodic flow over a Gaussian bump are analyzed to gain insight into turbulence modification under different pressure gradient regimes in three subregions. The four nonzero Reynolds stress components are defined in the local orthogonal coordinate system at a given location on the bump surface. The first subregion starts upstream of the bump under a mild adverse pressure gradient (APG) that becomes progressively stronger toward the bump. The second subregion succeeds the first subregion near the bump foot and contains a strong favorable pressure gradient (FPG) until very near the bump apex. The third subregion is the strong APG section that begins near the apex and lasts until the flow separation point. The mild/strong APG reduces the mean shear rate near the wall, which has a dampening effect on turbulence production while the strong FPG leads to an order of magnitude increase in near-wall turbulence production as a result of the much-enhanced mean shear rate.

Title: Modeling of Depth Cue Integration in Manual Control Tasks
Abstract: Psychophysical research has demonstrated that human observers utilize a variety of visual cues to form a perception of three-dimensional depth. However, most of these studies have utilized a passive judgement paradigm, and failed to consider depth-cue integration as a dynamic and task-specific process. In the current study, we developed and experimentally validated a model of manual control of depth that examines how two potential cues (stereo disparity and relative size) are utilized in both first- and second-order active depth control tasks. We found that stereo disparity plays the dominate role for determining depth position, while relative size dominates perception of depth velocity. Stereo disparity also plays a reduced role when made less salient (i.e., when viewing distance is increased). Manual control models predict that position information is sufficient for first-order control tasks, while velocity information is required to perform a second-order control task. Thus, the rules for depth-cue integration in active control tasks are dependent on both task demands and cue quality.

A weld is made in the FSW process by translating a rotating pin along a weld seam so as to stir the sides of the seam together. This article provides an introduction to the FSW process. The chief concern is the physical effect of the tool on the weld metal: how weld seam bonding takes place, what kind of weld structure is generated, potential problems, possible defects for example, and implications for process parameters and tool design. Weld properties are determined by structure, and the structure of friction stir welds is determined by the weld metal flow field in the vicinity of the weld tool. Metal flow in the vicinity of the weld tool is explained through a simple kinematic flow model that decomposes the flow field into three basic component flows: a uniform translation, a rotating solid cylinder, and a ring vortex encircling the tool.

Title: Ice Nucleation in the Tropical Tropopause Layer: Implications for Cirrus Occurrence, Cirrus Microphysical Properties, and Dehydration of Air Entering the Stratosphere
Abstract: Recent laboratory experiments have advanced our understanding of the physical properties and ice nucleating abilities of aerosol particles atlow temperatures. In particular, aerosols containing organics will transition to a glassy state at low temperatures, and these glassy aerosols are moderately effective as ice nuclei. These results have implications for ice nucleation in the cold Tropical Tropopause Layer (TTL; 13-19 km). We have developed a detailed cloud microphysical model that includes heterogeneous nucleation on a variety of aerosol types and homogeneous freezing of aqueous aerosols. The model includes scavenging of ice nuclei by sedimenting ice crystals. The model is evaluated by comparing the simulated cloud properties and water vapor concentrations with aircraft and satellite measurements. In this presentation, I will discuss the relative importance of homogeneous and heterogeneous ice nucleation, the impact of ice nuclei scavenging as air slowly ascends through the TTL, and the implications for the final dehydration of air parcels crossing the tropical cold-point tropopause and entering the tropical stratosphere.

Abstract: Past decades have seen an accelerating increase in computing efficiency, while climate models are representing a rapidly widening set of physical processes. Yet simulations of some fundamental aspects of climate like precipitation or aerosol forcing remain highly uncertain and resistant to progress. Dust aerosol modeling of soil particles lofted by wind erosion has seen a similar conflict between increasing model sophistication and remaining uncertainty. Dust aerosols perturb the energy and water cycles by scattering radiation and acting as ice nuclei, while mediating atmospheric chemistry and marine photosynthesis (and thus the carbon cycle). Representing this range leads to several modeling challenges. Should we limit complexity in our model, which consumes computer resources and inhibits interpretation? How do we decide if a process involving dust is worthy of inclusion within our model? Title: In Situ Strategy of the 2011 Mars Science Laboratory to Investigate the Habitability of Ancient Mars
Abstract: The ten science investigations of the 2011 Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Rover named "Curiosity" seek to provide a quantitative assessment of habitability through chemical and geological measurements from a highly capable robotic' platform. This mission seeks to understand if the conditions for life on ancient Mars are preserved in the near-surface geochemical record. These substantial payload resources enabled by MSL's new entry descent and landing (EDL) system have allowed the inclusion of instrument types nevv to the Mars surface including those that can accept delivered sample from rocks and soils and perform a wide range of chemical, isotopic, and mineralogical analyses. The Chemistry and Mineralogy (CheMin) experiment that is located in the interior of the rover is a powder x-ray Diffraction (XRD) and X-ray Fluorescence (XRF) instrument that provides elemental and mineralogical information. The Sample Analysis at Mars (SAM) suite of instruments complements this experiment by analyzing the volatile component of identically processed samples and by analyzing atmospheric composition.

NASA technical report (published 2014)
Title: Ground Operations Autonomous Control and Integrated Health Management
Abstract: An intelligent autonomous control capability has been developed and is currently being validated in ground cryogenic fluid management operations. The capability embodies a physical architecture consistent with typical launch infrastructure and control systems, augmented by a higher level autonomous control (AC) system enabled to make knowledge-based decisions. The AC system is supported by an integrated system health management (ISHM) capability that detects anomalies, diagnoses causes, determines effects, and could predict future anomalies. AC is implemented using the concept of programmed sequences that could be considered to be building blocks of more generic mission plans. A sequence is a series of steps, and each executes actions once conditions for the step are met (e.g. desired temperatures or fluid state are achieved). For autonomous capability, conditions must consider also health management outcomes, as they will determine whether or not an action is executed, or how an action may be executed, or if an alternative action is executed instead. Aside from health, higher level objectives can also drive how a mission is carried out.

NASA technical report (published 2003)
Title: Our Space Future: A Challenge to the Conceptual Artist Concept Art for Presentation and Education
Abstract: The history of visual representation is as old as the history of humankind. The Paleolithic drawings that are found in caves present our collective need for recording our dependence on the life-sustaining animal populations. Our wishes for their fertility (and for our own) comprise much of the art we find in these prehistoric drawings. As well, the cycles of the Moon are recorded in Paleolithic art relating to women's estrus cycles that link the perpetuation of our species with the cosmos. Art became our initial way of description and a way of envisioning our future goals. At the time when pictograms began to form humanity s first written languages, we also started to use art to invoke favorable forces and ward off devastation. Another important application of visual art became the conceptualization of tools, buildings and ideas that were impossible to describe by other means. Humans have a historical tradition of considering visual images as vehicles to inspire us to pursue a different way of thinking through our ability of envisioning. Complex concepts can be described visually and have the ability to convey information on many different levels.

Abstract: This work uses existing technologies to prepare a crossbar architecture of nano tubes, wherein one nanotube is fixed to a substrate, and a second nanotube is suspended a finite distance above. Both nano tubes can be individually addressed electrically. Application of opposite potentials to the two tubes causes the top tube to deform and to essentially come into contact with the lower tube. Contact here refers not to actual, physical contact, but rather within an infinitesimally small distance referred to as van der Walls contact, in which the entities may influence each other on a molecular and electronic scale. First, the top tube is physically deformed, leading to a potentially higher chemical reactivity at the point of deformation, based on current understanding of the effects of curvature strain on reactivity. This feature would allow selective functionalization at the junction via reaction with diazonium salts. Secondly, higher potential is achieved at the point of "cross" between the tubes.

Title: Health Monitoring of a Rotating Disk Using a Combined Analytical-Experimental Approach
Abstract: Rotating disks undergo rigorous mechanical loading conditions that make them subject to a variety of failure mechanisms leading to structural deformities and cracking. During operation, periodic loading fluctuations and other related factors cause fractures and hidden internal cracks that can only be detected via noninvasive types of health monitoring and/or nondestructive evaluation. These evaluations go further to inspect material discontinuities and other irregularities that have grown to become critical defects that can lead to failure. Hence, the objectives of this work is to conduct a collective analytical and experimental study to present a well-rounded structural assessment of a rotating disk by means of a health monitoring approach and to appraise the capabilities of an in-house rotor spin system. The analyses utilized the finite element method to analyze the disk with and without an induced crack at different loading levels, such as rotational speeds starting at 3000 up to 10 000 rpm. A parallel experiment was conducted to spin the disk at the desired speeds in an attempt to correlate the experimental findings with the analytical results.

Title: Interplanetary Sample Return Missions Using Radioisotope Electric Propulsion
Abstract: Radioisotope electric propulsion (REP) has recently been shown to effectively complement SEP and NEP for missions to high-AU targets with modest payload requirements. This paper investigates the application of an advanced REP for a sample return from the comet Tempel 1. A set of mission and system parameters are varied with the goal of quantifying their impact on total mission payload. Mission parameters considered include trip-time and Earth return entry interface speed of the sample return system. System parameters considered include launch vehicle, power level of spacecraft at beginning of mission, and thruster specific impulse. For the baseline case of Atlas 401 and REP power level of 750 W, the mission time was 12 years, the payload was 144 kg, and the missions optimized to a single specific impulse generally within Hall ion thruster range. Other cases were investigated in support of graduate studies, and include the larger Atlas 551 launch vehicle and extended power level to 1 kW. The Atlas 551 cases tended to optimize dual specific impulses generally in the Hall ion thruster range for both legs of the mission.
